msContents.summary: [p]De lapide philosophico operavaria dieversorum actorum fideliter collects. Mdlii [sic]. Pen-drawings of alchemical apparatus, schematic figures, etc. on ff. 3, 29, 30, 35, 54 of the first section. On the t.p. and at the end of each section a pen-drawn floral device. The date given on the general title as 'MDLII' seems to be possibly a mistake for 'MDCLII'. The Work by Arthur Dee (1579-1651] was first published in Paris in 1631, and later translated by Elias Ashmole, at London in 1650. In both these printed editions the Author does not mention his Father, the celebrated John Dee [1527-1608].[/p] [li]Pantheo, G.A. listBibl.bibl: The last work is discussed at length by Thorndike in his 'History of Magic and Experimental Science', Vol. III, pp. 182-190, 688-691, but he comes to no conclusion as to the authorship. Pantheo and his writings, are discussed in Vol. V, pp. 537--540, of the same work. From the style of writing, the alchem,ical poem, and other internal evidence, this MS. seems to have been written in Italy. It was composed by a 'Philosophus Aureae Crucis', but little information has been traced as to this Order, which may have had Rosicrucian connections. According to Waite in his 'Brotherhood of the Rosy Cross', p. 343, this name was also applied to that enigmatic Society. Waite also draws attention to the tract 'Aureum seculum redivivum', published in 1621 or 1622, and reissued in 1638 and 1645. This originally appeared under the name of 'Madathanus' which is known to be a pseudonym for Hadrianus a Mynsicht [1603-1638.]. In this tract the Author describes himself as 'Frater Aureae Crucis'.
